data.title: May 11, 2026 archive records show BGSU library retrieval and backend-port/routing probes through proxies. Public catalogue content was returned; successful bypass, private-data access and AI authorship are unproven.
data.summary:
Arquivo records show public library retrieval alongside possible backend reconnaissance and routing workarounds at Bowling Green State University (BGSU). Successful bypass, private-data access and AI authorship are unproven.

Scope: 11 May 2026, 17:14:53–21:00:43 UTC. The reviewed export contains 170 URL-and-capture-time pairs covering 159 URL strings: 169 through r.jina.ai and one through markdown.new. Capture counts do not establish independent users, actual origin requests or a common actor.

Observed sequence

- Backend-port probes: Five captures between 18:32:47 and 18:33:03 target lib.bgsu.edu on ports 8089 and 8081, including /repositories/3/resources and /version, plus 129.1.14.56:8089/version. All five have indexed proxy status 422. ArchivesSpace documents these default ports and the /version route, making backend discovery plausible; actual service exposure and delivery remain unknown.

- Route variations: 72 captured URLs contain container identifier 8059. Variants change case, HTTP/HTTPS, slashes, suffixes, query values and proxy nesting. Nine use top_containers;/8059 and 18 use rnd= values. This suggests systematic attempts to find a readable route, but ordinary catalogue navigation explains some requests and bypass intent is uncertain.

- Public content: Fourteen preserved response bodies include library pages, robots.txt and public finding aids for the Jacqueline Deegan Papers (MUSIC-030; repository 3, resource 768). The collection overview says it is open for research. No underlying private papers or personal account records are demonstrated.

- Access policy: The robots.txt capture disallows top-container and resource-tree paths for User-agent: *. This does not establish an authentication boundary, prove that a requester read it, or identify an AI provider.

Outcome and limitations

Indexed proxy statuses: 137 with 401; 16 with 200; 7 with 403; 6 with 422; 3 with 301; and 1 with 500. Most failed response bodies are missing, so these errors cannot be attributed specifically to the university. The rejecting component could be a proxy, intermediary or target. One /tree capture has indexed status 200 but its preserved text reports upstream 404.

No credentials, authenticated session, successful bypass, private-data access, modification or caused outage are demonstrated. Automation is plausible, but human scripting remains possible. AI company: Unknown.

Evidence guide

The eight links below are in this order:
1. Hostname-based backend-port probe, 18:32:47 UTC.
2. IP-based /version probe, 18:33:03 UTC.
3. Preserved robots.txt capture, 18:34:09 UTC.
4. Public collection finding aid, 18:36:20 UTC.
5. Semicolon route variation, 19:29:24 UTC.
6. ArchivesSpace API documentation.
7. ArchivesSpace default port configuration.
8. ARIN registration for the IP range containing 129.1.14.56. Current registration does not independently prove a historical hostname-to-IP mapping.

Some archive replay links may no longer resolve. The companion evidence ZIP contains all 170 event records and a chronological timeline, 14 original exported response files with source metadata, exact native archive-index rows, and checksums. It also retains the other capture URLs omitted from this shorter link list.

Evidence verification

The 14 response files match our saved export and reconstructed source text, but their hashes differ from the original archive-index digests. Their exact identity with the original archived payloads remains unverified. Verification details are included in original-export/body-verification.json in the ZIP.
